review_text:
Date of Visit: 15 July 2025 - Review of Aster Hospital Emergency Services - RATE 1 - 10
Patient ID: 900631438

I would like to share my recent and disappointing experience at Aster Hospital’s Emergency Department in the Mankhool branch.

We arrived at the emergency reception around 5:30 PM, and although it was clearly an emergency (I was in severe abdominal pain), we were only attended to around 5:50 PM—a 20-minute wait despite being in obvious distress. This delay was unacceptable in an emergency setting, especially when patients are supposed to receive immediate attention.

Once I was finally placed on a bed, the doctor examined me, administered a pain reliever, and recommended further tests, including a CT scan of the abdomen and pelvis, an IV drip, and blood tests. Despite these steps, I felt neglected throughout the evening. I vomited severely at 11:45 PM and requested to be admitted to a room to rest more comfortably, but that also took a long time. It wasn’t until around 4:00 AM that the CT scan was done, after which I begged again for a room, and was finally moved to Room 406—only after vomiting again.

I must commend one compassionate nurse in the room who truly showed care, his name, Allwin Jeffry - unlike the staff in the emergency room, who lacked empathy and made me feel like a burden instead of a patient in need.

Later in the morning, I requested to be discharged so I could travel to Jordan for treatment with my longtime doctor. I asked for my medical release at 8:30 AM, but even this simple request took an unreasonable amount of time. Although we settled the AED 200 excess payment quickly, the staff delayed my discharge by claiming the printer wasn’t working and insisted I stay in the room—despite everything being settled and my ID already returned.

One male staff member in pink uniform even acted rudely, which made the situation worse. I told him that I was not a prisoner to be held unnecessarily. My driver had to rush through the stairs with proof of payment to ensure I wouldn’t miss my 2 PM flight to Jordan all because of the inefficient discharge process. please review your camera, and he must be given extra seminar on how to handle customer care! this is must for him!

This experience was not only physically painful but also emotionally exhausting!!! I am deeply disappointed by the lack of urgency, care, and compassion shown in the emergency department. Aster Hospital is a large and reputable name, yet this experience was far from what a patient should expect in an emergency medical facility!

I sincerely hope the hospital takes this feedback seriously and works to improve its emergency protocols, discharge procedures, and staff attitude toward patients in pain. No one should have to suffer in such a way while seeking help in a hospital.

Unfortunately, I will not return to this hospital again. Please, train your staff to treat every patient with respect, care, and urgency especially those in critical conditions.

I’ve always had pleasant experiences at Aster Hospital, Mankhool in the past, but my recent visit left me somewhat disappointed.

On 04/10/2025, I requested a replacement vaccination card for my daughter after misplacing the original. I paid the required fees, and the Pediatric Department informed me that I would receive a call once the document was ready. However, I did not receive any follow-up.

By 08/10/2025, still having heard nothing, I contacted the call center, where I was assured the relevant department had been informed and that I would receive a call soon. After another two days without any response, I called again and received the same message.

Due to the lack of communication, I visited the hospital in person on 11/10/2025, expecting the card to be ready given the time that had passed. To my surprise, the request was still pending. I was told that the doctors had not had time to complete the required information, which was frustrating.

After I escalated the matter, the Patient Coordinators stepped in and addressed the issue. I was told the vaccination card would be ready in three days. On 16/10/2025, I finally received a call confirming it was ready for collection.

While I appreciate the support provided by the patient coordination team once the matter was raised, I would like to highlight the need for improvement in the call center's communication and follow-up process.

NB: This review is based on my personal experience—others may have a smoother and more positive experience.

I have been a loyal patient at Mediclinic for over four years. In the past, my experience was excellent, and I trusted your services fully. Unfortunately, over the last two years, the quality of care at City Hospital has declined significantly. I am compelled to raise the following concerns:

1. Misdiagnosis and Negligence (Husband’s Case)
Two years ago, my husband visited the hospital due to bleeding. After a check-up, the doctor concluded that “all is fine.” Recently, we discovered he has gallbladder stones, which by now have grown so large they cannot be dissolved. This represents a clear case of medical negligence. Despite submitting a formal complaint, the representative who contacted us excused and defended the doctor instead of acknowledging responsibility. Until today, no corrective action has been taken.

2. Emergency Visit – Broken Sample and Lack of Communication
I visited the emergency department with severe pain, fever, and diarrhea. I was discharged and asked to leave stool samples for testing. After 15 days, during another appointment, I was informed that the test results never came out because the sample containers were broken. No one contacted me to inform me of this failure, leaving my condition untreated and unresolved.

3. Influenza Diagnosis – Missing Critical Prescription
Two days ago, I was admitted again with 40.2°C fever, chest pain, cough, headache, and body pain. I was diagnosed with influenza, and the doctor clearly stated Tamiflu would be prescribed. However, upon reviewing my medications later, I realized Tamiflu was never given — despite being the primary treatment for influenza. This is a serious error that put my health at risk.

4. Pediatrician department
We came running with our baby with high fever to see if we can get a walking appointment, Pediatrician replied to us: "go to emergency because I am in a photo shooting right now" in this a proper and professional answer?

5. General Decline in Patient Care
While there are a few excellent doctors who truly care for their patients, many others appear to treat patients as tasks, without empathy or proper attention. Often, patients feel rushed or dismissed instead of being properly heard. This mechanical, “robotic” approach is very concerning, because we aren't taking this health service for free,  through our insurance a lot of money has been paid.

6. Cultural Representation of Staff
Given Dubai’s multicultural environment, I strongly recommend Mediclinic consider hiring more doctors and nurses from diverse nationalities. Patients often feel more comfortable expressing sensitive issues in a culturally familiar environment, which would improve trust and satisfaction.

These repeated incidents reflect a pattern of negligence, poor communication, and lack of accountability. Mediclinic was once a trusted name for my family, but my recent experiences at City Hospital have left us deeply disappointed and concerned for our safety as patients.

I urge you to take immediate corrective action, investigate these cases properly, and ensure higher standards of patient care are restored. Otherwise, you risk losing the trust of long-standing patients like myself.

None of the recommendations seemed baseless or refutable and were easy to implement…. Loved the open conversation, your energy and passion into this topic. Would highly recommend you to my friends and family, since Diet is no longer a health topic but a well-being one…. Can’t thank you enough!! 🙏

I have been going to Mediclinic City Hospital. for my follow up check-ups. As a history I had to undergo a brain procedure where they had to insert a flow diverter stent in my right carotid artery. This will avoid  the artery from rupturing thus preventing stroke. Dr. Kassem El Shunnar is the best in his field. He was able to give me a very clear explanation about the status of my stent and its progress. He is very caring and intentional to his patients. I would also thank his nurse Ms. Lerma for also assisting my needs and even calling me to update on my requests. They also have the best Neuroradiologist Dr. Rosario Papa. He handled my case with utmost professionalism and genuine care. Very skilled in his chosen craft.

And of course how could II forget my Nephrologist Dr. Imane Guermah. From the time I met her and took my case we felt her genuine care and love. She is very intentional checking on me by whatsapp messaging my wife. Checking my BP, food intake and even my sleep. She already made a plan on how to take care of my kidneys. And did I mention that it was through her initiative to get my brain MRI  that the aneurysm in my brain was found out and was treated. That shows her tremendous knowledge about her chosen field. She gave us inspiration to even train my eldest daughter to be a Nephro like her.

Everyday I thank God for these people who are taking good care of me. Grateful to have met them and very happy with the care they are giving me. God bless you all.

review_text:
This review is directed to Mediclinic City Hospital and Dr. Amel Ginawi, because the behavior of her nurse, Sunitha Poola, was absolutely disgraceful and unfit for any medical setting.

I had an appointment as a new patient at 11:40 AM. After checking in properly and being told by the main receptionist that I was next, another woman with a 12:40 PM appointment walked in and was allowed to go in before me not because of any emergency, but simply because Snuthi Poola decided she was more important. The nurse blatantly dismissed protocol, was laughing in the hallway with the other patient, and took me in for just 3 minutes to check weight/height, and in that moment, I told her clearly that I had tested positive for lupus a serious autoimmune disease that can affect vital organs. Her response? She still told me to wait for the other patient to finish. No concern. No urgency. No triage. Nothing.

When I confronted her, she didn’t apologize instead, she argued, made excuses, and claimed the other patient was “an existing customer,” as if that justifies completely ignoring the appointment schedule.
Worse, she lied and said the patient was dizzy even though no mention of dizziness was made at reception, and even if it were true, it has nothing to do with seeing a rheumatologist. Dizziness is not an urgent symptom in a rheumatology clinic. If it were a true emergency, the patient should have been sent to urgent care or a different specialty, not allowed to cut the line under a false excuse. That explanation was clearly a cover-up for blatant favoritism and unprofessionalism.

To make things worse, the nurse knew I was in a hurry, and if she had any true concern for patient well-being, she would have considered that I was coming in for a serious health issue, not a basic check-up. She had no idea what condition I was being seen for, and for all she knew, my case could have been far more urgent than the other patient’s. Her decision to ignore that and prioritize someone simply because they were a “regular” shows just how irresponsible and unprofessional she truly is.

I’ve been an existing customer myself at another Hospital won’t mention its name and I have never once seen a new patient get sidelined like this. Her behavior was rude, condescending, and dishonest. She treated me like I was too dumb to understand how the system works when in reality, she was the one breaking it.

The rest of the nursing staff were no better not one stepped in, and their body language clearly showed they were annoyed I was even speaking up. The only two people who acted with decency were the main receptionist, who initially said it was my turn, and the nurse manager, who kindly stepped in after everything and tried to salvage the situation. Honestly, she doesn’t deserve to work in a place where patients are ignored, dismissed, and treated like they’re in the way.

Snuthi Poola’s attitude, dishonesty, and lack of basic professionalism is unacceptable. I walked out completely disrespected, with no apology from her, and I will never return. If this is how Dr. Amel Ginawi’s staff treats patients, especially new ones, then I strongly do not recommend this hospital to anyone.

I truly have more words but no words can explain my disappointment and how my health was dismissed by the nurse!

**Thank You Note:**

I would like to extend my heartfelt thanks to Dr. Asim Rafiq, the best surgeon at Thumbay Hospital. During my discharge, he was there, and his presence meant a lot to me. Dr. Asim Rafiq, you are truly the best.

Dr. Asim Rafiq is so nice and speaks so well. I felt very comfortable with him as he explained my situation and the surgery details very clearly. His calm demeanor and thorough explanations were incredibly reassuring. Even now, while I am still in recovery, he has provided his mobile number so I can reach out to him if I need urgent assistance. He truly is the best doctor.

I would also like to express my gratitude to all the nurses who took care of me on June 22-23, 2024. Your dedication and care made a significant difference in my recovery. God bless all of you for the incredible work you do.

A special thank you to the staff members who accompanied me to my room after the recovery room and sometimes brought food to my room. I really appreciate the two individuals, one man and one woman, who checked on me and ensured I was comfortable. Your kindness did not go unnoticed. Wow, you are the best too!

A heartfelt thank you to the anesthesiologist as well. He was incredibly attentive during the surgery, noticing that I was feeling cold and promptly providing some form of heating, which helped me feel comfortable again. His care, along with the assistance of the nurses in the surgery room, was deeply appreciated. I also want to thank the nurse and the lady nurses in the surgery room; although I can't recall how many there were, they were all very kind and supportive.

Additionally, I had surgery in February 2024 with Dr. Kapil Das, and he was exceptional as well. Thumbay Hospital is my go-to place whenever I am not feeling well, and I am grateful for the consistently excellent care I receive.

Thank you to everyone at Thumbay Hospital in Nuaimiya, Ajman, UAE.

---
BEST REGARDS,
ERMA MAE MONTILLA ABIERA

I am writing to formally express my deep disappointment with the services, communication, and overall patient handling at your facility during my recent visit. My experience has been frustrating, stressful, and, frankly, unacceptable for a healthcare institution.

On July 9, I visited the hospital for a consultation with a urology doctor. During this visit, I was advised to undergo additional tests, including blood tests for creatinine and urea, and a CT scan. That evening, I received a call from the radiology department to confirm the CT scan request. I informed them I was still waiting for my lab results, which were eventually sent later that night.

The following morning, I called to confirm the CT scan schedule and inquired about the necessary preparations. Unfortunately, the staff member I spoke with provided unclear and confusing information. When I asked specifically about what preparation was required, they simply said “nothing,” without elaboration.

I also booked an appointment with the urology doctor for 2:30 PM to review my lab results before proceeding with the scan. I arrived at 2:00 PM only to be told the doctor was still in surgery and would not return until 3:30 PM. The doctor eventually arrived at 4:00 PM. This shows a clear lack of coordination—if the doctor was unavailable, why was a 2:30 PM slot confirmed?

During the consultation, the doctor briefly reviewed my results and instructed me to proceed with the CT scan—again with no guidance or explanation.

When I went to radiology, I was informed for the first time that the CT scan required contrast and that fasting was necessary. At this point, I felt completely let down. I had not been told anything about fasting, and due to my last meal being at 12:00 PM, I had to wait until 6:00 PM for the procedure.

Even after returning at 6:00 PM, the delays continued. A nurse inserted an IV line at around 6:30 PM, and I waited another 90 minutes for the radiologist. At 8:00 PM, I was finally called in—only to face another delay because my information had not been entered into the system. It was disorganized and stressful. One radiologist was handling both MRI and CT scans, leading to a long queue. I finally completed the procedure at 9:00 PM.

This entire experience—from poor communication and scheduling, to lack of clear instructions, understaffing, and long waiting times—reflects a system that is inefficient and inconsiderate of patients’ time, comfort, and emotional well-being. Once payment is made, it feels as though the patient is left to navigate a chaotic system on

This has been the worst experience I have had in a hospital, and I am left feeling frustrated and uncared for. I hope you will take this complaint seriously and address the systemic issues affecting patient care.
